text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape resembled NVDA's current state, the median realised return over the next 5 sessions was 0.86%. The distribution is wide and slightly right-skewed, with a standard deviation of 3.8%, meaning the path through the week matters as much as the endpoint.

[state]
The retrieval engine pulled these 50 analogs because several features are simultaneously elevated. WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) sits at 19.24% with a z-score of 1.124, the most extreme feature in the set. NVDA's own 20-session realised volatility (vol20) is 45.77% (z: 0.824), and the mean absolute overnight/weekend gap (gap20) is 1.28% (z: 0.718). The stock is -6.03% from its 52-week high (dist52, z: 0.564) after a 60-session return of 11.82%. Meanwhile, benchmark 20-session volatility (mktVol20) is unusually quiet at 9.16% (z: -0.574), and 20-session dollar volume (dv20z) is below average at a z-score of -0.62. There are 45 calendar days to the next earnings release (dte) and 0 scheduled events in the next 5 sessions (eventLoad5). This combination of high idiosyncratic volatility, an oil shock, and a quiet broad market pulls in a mix of energy names, tech peers, and recent 2025-2026 sessions.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of 0.65% and a median of 0.86%. The spread is substantial: the 10th percentile is -4.04%, the 25th percentile is -2.03%, the 75th percentile is 3.07%, and the 90th percentile is 4.68%. The extremes range from -7.34% to 10.25%, with a skew of 0.214. In 56% of the episodes the return was above zero, and in 44% it was below. Six of the 50 episodes (12%) finished worse than -5%, and none reached -10%. The bad tail is dominated by specific recent sessions. The closest match is NVDA itself on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2999), which returned -5.9% over 5 sessions with a max adverse excursion of -7.44%. XLK on 2026-08-13 (distance 0.4178) returned -4.02%. On the upside, NVDA on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.4317) returned 9.66%, and MU on 2024-01-16 (distance 0.4111) returned 3.45%. The Technology sector accounts for 9 of the 50 analogs, while 2025 and 2026 together account for 38 of them.

[tails]
A position can end near the median and still be difficult to hold through the week. Across the 50 analogs, the median maximum adverse excursion was -2.01%. At the 25th percentile, the worst intra-week drawdown was -3.77%, and at the 10th percentile it was -4.38%. The median maximum favourable excursion was 2.55%, reaching 4.39% at the 75th percentile and 6.71% at the 90th percentile, giving a reward/risk ratio of 1.27. Looking at specific drawdown thresholds, 8 of the 50 episodes breached a 5% drawdown during the 5 sessions. None breached 10%, 15%, or 20%.

[stress]
Fourteen stress scenarios were run; none were skipped. Against the baseline median of 0.86%, several windows materially worsen the picture. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario produced a median forward return of -5.4% across 48 analogs, a delta of -6.26% versus baseline, with a 10th percentile of -14.14% and a 58.3% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns, making it a sample of one regime rather than a forecast. The 2018-Q4 tightening scare yielded a median of -3.02% (delta -3.88%) over 50 analogs, with a 90th percentile of -0.19%; its caveat is that it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters late-window analogs. The 2022 inflation/rate bear produced a median of -2.42% (delta -3.28%) over 50 analogs; its caveat is that a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind showed a median of -2.11% (delta -2.97%) over 36 analogs, with a 10th percentile of -8.61%; its caveat is that the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2025-04 tariff shock gave a median of -2.7% (delta -3.56%) over 26 analogs; its caveat is that policy reversals inside the window make the tail asymmetric in a way specific to that episode. Among shocks, the Volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX) produced a median of -0.18% (delta -1.04%) over 50 analogs; its caveat is that VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, stressing entry timing more than terminal value. The Liquidity air pocket scenario had a median of 0.83% (delta -0.03%) over 50 analogs, but its caveat notes that for the verified NVDA/USDT Bitget RWA perpetual, the reference market is closed for 81.4% of the week and 54.59% of its realised hourly movement happened in those closed hours, so the gap risk described is not hypothetical. The Weekend hold on the 7x24 venue scenario produced a median of 0.39% (delta -0.47%) over 50 analogs; its caveat is that blocks are paired to analogs by index modulo the block count, a deterministic convention rather than a joint distribution, and the measured window holds only a handful of distinct weekends, so blocks are cross-correlated.

[reasoning]
The three scenarios most relevant to this idea are the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash, because its median of -5.4% and 58.3% breach probability over 48 analogs show what happens when the high realised volatility (45.77%) meets a systemic bid-ask blowout; the 2024-08-05 carry unwind, because its 10th percentile of -8.61% over 36 analogs isolates the gap risk implied by the 1.28% mean absolute overnight gap; and the Volatility spike shock, because its median of -0.18% over 50 analogs directly conditions on the vol complex re-pricing, which is the primary risk given the divergence between NVDA's 45.77% vol and the benchmark's 9.16%. A concentration to distrust is the heavy weighting of 2025 and 2026 sessions, which together supply 38 of the 50 analogs, potentially over-fitting the distribution to the most recent regime. No scenario contradicts the direction of a long idea by producing a strongly positive median; all negative scenarios align with downside risk.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The honest verdict from the engine's validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The conformal interval achieves 80.8% out-of-sample coverage with a width of 10.4%, but the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -7.6%, meaning the naive benchmark is tighter at the same coverage. For path risk, the engine targets a 10% drawdown level. Out of sample, the realised breach rate was 2%, while the mean predicted rate from the analog excursion share was 3.4%, yielding a calibration gap of 1.4 percentage points with a clustered standard error of 0.48. The analog Brier score (MAE) was 0.0196, compared to 0.0241 for the volatility reflection benchmark, 0.024 for the same-name calibration, and 0.021 for the pooled calibration. The paired Brier differences resolve in favour of the analog against all three benchmarks, as the 95% confidence intervals do not span zero: versus vol reflection [-0.0071, -0.0022], versus same-name [-0.0059, -0.0029], and versus pooled [-0.0023, -0.0005]. Regarding the wrapper, the status is measured on the primary venue, the Bitget official MCP (NVDA/USDT RWA perpetual). The reference cash market is shut for 81.4% of the week, and 54.59% of the wrapper's own hourly movement landed in those closed hours. It is graded a fair tracker with a return correlation of 0.8988 and a tracking error of 111 bp/day. The basis band is -0.37% to 0.66%, and the spread is 0.44 bps. The wrapper caveat is that a fair perpetual is not the underlying and not a redeemable spot token: at 111 bp/day of tracking error it carries its own idiosyncratic risk, funding applies, and the basis band means the exit price can differ from the reference close the analog distribution is built on. For the return layer, 6 weekend blocks were observed on Bitget. The median weekend block return was 0.428%, the 10th percentile was -1.3695%, and the standard deviation was 1.4103%. The median intra-weekend adverse excursion was -0.8185%, and 0% of those 6 weekends breached the 5% drawdown threshold. These are wrapper returns measured while the reference market was shut and NOT the retrieved outcome distribution above, which is built on 5x24 daily sessions.
